messages.subject: Literature on grouping species detections
parts:
Hi all,

I am currently working on my camera trap study on the occurrence of large ungulates: white-lipped peccary, lowland tapir and brocket deer (Mazama spp), in logging concessions in Guyana. I have mostly 1s in my detection history for each species and when I used 1-day as my sampling occasion in my single season, single species occupancy models, they resulted in errors. I realised that I may have to group my species observations since they occur quite frequently in my sites. Are there any literature that can provide information/recommendations on how best to group detection occasions for common species and the pros and cons of grouping? I have seen from previous posts that 3-7 days seem to be the most common grouping.

Thank you for the help!

Cheers,
Huichang

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Literature on grouping species detections
parts:
Dear Huichang,

what do you mean by "mostly 1s" ? That you detected the species (almost) everywhere ? If that is the case, then there is not much modeling of occupancy (as opposed to detection prob.) that can be done. When occupancy is constant at 1, then there is no variation to be explained by covariates, and all that may perhaps be explained is variation in detection. Grouping will then not help, because it will create even more occasions with detections (rather than nondetections) than the original data with 1-day resolution.

Grouping is usually done for computational and statistical reasons: you cut down the sample size along the temporal dimension and you increase detection probability per occasion.

Sorry to be the bearer of bad news ....

Marc

Dear Marc,

Not at all. This was super useful and interesting. I managed to produce (unsurprisingly) insignificate occupancy estimates for models with covariates (trail type, elevation, presence/absence of certain land use activities), after grouping into 6-days sampling occasion as opposed to the 1-day, which gave errors. 

Anyway, thank you. I suppose I will go tackle detection probabilties now.

Cheers,
Huichang
